description.value: The study tested whether sweet taste potentiates the reinforcing effects of nicotine in e-cigarettes by measuring conditioned flavor ratings and fMRI brain responses in light cigarette smokers.

spans.text: We therefore tested whether sweet taste potentiates the reinforcing effects of nicotine.

description.value: Sixteen light cigarette smokers underwent flavor conditioning with four e-cigarette conditions across repeated exposure days, followed by fMRI testing.

spans.text: Participants completed 2 exposure days per e-cigarette condition for a total of 8 exposure days within 2–3 weeks.

definition.value: sight of the sweet-paired e-cigarettes compared with control e-cigarettes

value: A stronger BOLD response in the NAcc to the sight of the sweet-paired e-cigarettes was observed compared with the control e-cigarettes, indicating that sweet taste increased conditioned cue-reactivity.

definition.value: a supra-additive response in the NAcc to the sight of the e-cigarette paired with sweet+nicotine

spans.text: Supporting our primary hypothesis, we observed a supra-additive response in the NAcc to the sight of the e-cigarette paired with sweet+nicotine versus the e-cigarettes paired with sweet or nicotine alone.

value: A supra-additive response was observed in the NAcc to the sight of the e-cigarette paired with sweet+nicotine, showing that sweet taste potentiated nicotine-related reinforcement signals.
